edits.old: Total project cost at appraisal was US$169.95 million.
edits.new: Total project cost at appraisal was US$169.70 million in the completion report's cost annex, Annex 1, and in the Independent Evaluation Group's own text; US$169.95 million is the figure the review's data sheet prints in its Total Project Cost field.

sichuan-small-towns-unfinished-resettlem.why: The US$169.95m figure is the IEG data sheet field only. The ICR's Annex 1 gives Total Project Costs 169.70 at appraisal (141.81 actual) and the IEG review's own text says 'The total appraisal estimate for this project was US$169.7 million'. Column named.

edits.old: Total project cost US$88,911,821 against US$86,560,000 at appraisal.
edits.new: Total project cost US$88,911,821 actually disbursed against US$86,560,000 in the original column of the report's financing table - a figure the report itself disowns in a note saying that the original Total Project Cost should be US$130.78 million as reported in the appraisal document and that the amount could not be fixed in the Bank's portal.

qufu-gupan-pond-demolition.why: ICR p.5 note: 'the original Non-World Bank Financing (Borrower) should be US$80.78 million, and the original Total Project Cost should be US$130.78 million, as reported in the PAD. The amount could not be fixed in the portal by the team.' Quoting 86,560,000 as the appraisal cost without that note is misleading.

edits.old: Environmental category A.
edits.new: Environmental category B, partial assessment.

edits.old: the Liaoning Urban Construction and Renewal Project Office, the same provincial office that ran the Bank's earlier Liaoning Medium Cities loans
edits.new: the Liaoning Urban Construction and Renewal Project Office, named in the completion report's data sheet; the appraisal document names the Liaoning Provincial Development and Reform Commission as the responsible agency

liaoning-coastal-zone-resettlement.why: ICR data sheet: Original EA Category and Revised EA Category both 'Partial Assessment (B)'; PAD basic information: 'EA Category B - Partial Assessment'. Category A was wrong. | No cited document says this office ran the earlier Liaoning Medium Cities projects; the ICR says only that this project 'followed four World Bank-financed urban environmental projects in Liaoning' and that their lessons were used (para 70). The PAD names a different responsible agency, which belongs on the card.

edits.old: lowered Bank performance to Moderately Satisfactory, finding the design fell short in two areas
edits.new: lowered both Bank performance and borrower performance to Moderately Satisfactory, finding that the design fell short in two areas and that the implementing agency's performance had shortcomings

second-shandong-environment-resettlement.why: IEG review's ratings table lowers borrower performance to Moderately Satisfactory as well as Bank performance. Reporting one of the two downgrades left the sentence misleading about what the review did.

edits.old: The report records that one reason the closing date was extended was delay in land acquisition and resettlement.
edits.new: The Independent Evaluation Group's review records that at the January 2016 restructuring the closing date was extended to 31 July 2016 because of the delays in land acquisition and resettlement; the completion report attributes the 23-month extension to the changes made to the Wuhu component.

luan-huaibei-urban-transport-resettlemen.why: The statement is in the IEG review ('because of the delays in land acquisition and resettlement, the loan closing date was extended to July 31, 2016'), not in the completion report, which ties the 23-month extension to the 2015 Wuhu restructuring (para 47) and records the land-acquisition delays separately (paras 49-50).

edits.old: The loan triggered the Bank's policies on involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12) and safety of dams (OP 4.37).
edits.new: The loan triggered five of the Bank's operational policies: environmental assessment (OP 4.01), natural habitats (OP 4.04), pest management (OP 4.09), involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12) and safety of dams (OP 4.37).

sichuan-wudu-canal-resettlement.why: ICR para 63 lists five triggered policies. Naming two of the five read as the full list.

edits.old: The loan triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment, physical cultural resources and involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12).
edits.new: The appraisal document records four safeguard policies triggered: environmental assessment (OP 4.01), physical cultural resources (OP 4.11), indigenous peoples (OP 4.10) and involuntary resettlement (OP 4.12).

yining-urban-roads-demolition.why: PAD safeguards table and para 1309 give four triggered policies, including Indigenous Peoples OP 4.10 - material on a card about demolition in the Yili Kazakh prefecture seat. The ICR names none.

edits.old: was approved 14 February 2012 as a separate project number
edits.new: was approved by the Bank's Board in February 2012, the completion report giving no day and its data sheet recording the associated restructuring on 10 February 2012, as a separate project number

rogun-stage1-resettlement.why: No cited document gives 14 February 2012. The ICR says 'In February 2012, the Bank's Board of Directors approved an Additional Financing'; its data sheet lists the restructuring as 02/10/2012; the additional financing project paper is dated 19 January 2012.

edits.old: with the loan and guarantee agreements signed 12 June 2007
edits.new: declared effective 17 August 2007; the 12 June 2007 signing date is the Bank's catalogue field, not a date given by any document cited here

santa-fe-road-19-expropriation.why: No cited document (ICR, ICRR, PAD, two Inspection Panel investigation reports) carries a 12 June 2007 signing date. The ICR gives approval 13 February 2007 and effectiveness 17 August 2007 on both its data sheet and in its text (para at p.722).

edits.old: The implementing agencies were the Tanzania National Roads Agency and the Tanzania Airports Authority.
edits.new: The completion report's data sheet names only the Tanzania National Roads Agency as implementing agency; the report adds that TANROADS was the principal implementing agency and handled overall coordination, while the Tanzania Airports Authority implemented the regional airports under Component B and the Government of Zanzibar the Zanzibar airport.

bukoba-airport-resettlement-arrears.why: ICR para 57: 'Although TANROADS was identified as the principal implementing agency for the project, many other GoT and GoZ agencies had responsibility for implementing various components (TAA for Component B-regional airports, GoZ for Component B-Zanzibar airport, two separate Divisions within the MoWTC for Components C and D).' The two-agency sentence was not what the Bank's records say.

xian-weiyang-xinjiamiao-resettlement.why: The completion report's cover prints Report No: ICR00004124. ICR00004130 appears nowhere in the document.

edits.old: alongside two other Chinese urban transport projects
edits.new: alongside the Bank's first and third Wuhan urban transport projects, approved in March 2004 and in 2012, to draw lessons on city-wide engagement

wuhan-nanhu-village-resettlement-delay.why: The review's assessment note is about the three Wuhan projects in the same city ('The field assessment of this and the other two projects can provide important lessons on city-wide engagement'), not about Chinese urban transport projects generally.

edits.old: 73 electric bus charging points and a relocated passenger station, and moved
edits.new: 73 electric bus charging stations and 1,648 on-board passenger-flow units, and moved

xining-wusixi-road-demolition.why: ICR para 12b lists the added items as 73 electric bus charging stations and 1,648 on-board bus units (passenger flow analysis systems), plus the interchange relocation and the dropping of two access roads. No relocated passenger station was added by the restructuring in any cited document.

edits.old: with additional financing of US$33 million approved 4 December 2008 under a separate project number, P110954
edits.new: with additional financing of US$33 million under a separate project number, P110954, for which the completion report cites a project paper of 6 November 2008 (the 4 December 2008 approval date is the Bank's catalogue field, not a date in the documents cited here)

edits.old: US$455.97 million actual, 132 per cent over
edits.new: US$455.97 million actual, which the report's cost table records as 132 per cent of the revised 2008 estimate of US$343.18 million

edits.old: and both rated risk to development outcome High
edits.new: and the review's table prints the risk to development outcome as High in both columns, where the completion report itself rates that risk Substantial

amman-development-corridor-land.why: No cited document gives 4 December 2008; the ICR's footnote cites 'World Bank Project Paper on Additional Financing for US$ 33 million, November 6, 2008'. | 132 is the 'Percentage of 2008 Appraisal' column against the revised estimate of US$343.18 million, not an overrun on the 2004 appraisal estimate (against which the actual cost was about 284 per cent). | ICR section 4: 'Rating: Substantial'. The High in the ICR column of the review's table is the review's own entry, not the report's rating.

edits.old: because incorporating bus rapid transit into the James Gichuru junction to Rironi section required wider resettlement areas and land acquisition
edits.new: because incorporating bus rapid transit into the JKIA to Rironi road section required wider resettlement areas and land acquisition

nutrip-road-compensation-arrears.why: ICR para 53 names the JKIA-Rironi road section (the 53 km JKIA-James Gichuru-Rironi corridor); James Gichuru-Rironi is the 26 km funded part of it.

edits.old: Total project cost was US$215 million.
edits.new: Total project cost was US$215.99 million at appraisal against US$193.01 million actual.

qiantang-small-town-house-demolition.why: The report's cost annex gives appraisal 215.99 and actual 193.01. The single unlabelled figure was the appraisal column and read as the project's cost.

edits.old: Credits IDA-50110 of US$70 million and IDA-53070 of US$32 million for the National Water Resources Development Project (P107350), approved 15 September 2011.
edits.new: Credits IDA-50110 of US$70 million and IDA-53070 of US$32 million for the National Water Resources Development Project (P107350). The project and the first credit were approved 15 September 2011; IDA-53070 was the additional financing approved at the first restructuring on 27 September 2013, for emergency rehabilitation after the flooding in southern Mozambique.

corumana-dam-resettlement-mozambique.why: ICR para 10: the first restructuring was approved on September 27, 2013 as part of an Additional Financing of SDR 21.2 million (US$32 million equivalent). The single 15 September 2011 approval date covered both credits.

edits.old: The project financing agreement was revised to include the provisions of
edits.new: The project's Environment and Social Management Framework was revised to include the provisions of

patna-ganga-riverfront-resettlement.why: ICR para 21: 'Changes in Environment and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and sewer network investments: The ESMF was revised to include provisions made under the RFCTLAR&R Act 2013'. The financing agreement was not revised for this.

edits.old: the Independent Evaluation Group's review rated it Satisfactory, citing weak evidence of sanitation sustainability and the project's efficiency, and noted moderate shortcomings in procurement and in the implementation of safeguard policies that delayed the project
edits.new: the Independent Evaluation Group's review rated outcome Satisfactory, rating efficacy substantial because the evidence of sanitation sustainability was weak and efficiency substantial, and lowered Bank performance to Moderately Satisfactory, finding moderate shortcomings at entry in identifying the risks related to procurement and to safeguards policy implementation and a results framework that did not adequately capture the project's outputs and outcomes

ouagadougou-onea-works-before-compensati.why: The review's reason column gives those shortcomings as its grounds for lowering Bank performance from Satisfactory to Moderately Satisfactory, which the role omitted; and it rates both efficacy and efficiency substantial rather than finding the efficiency evidence weak.
